messages.author: 6b13d9fbd0ae7797
messages.subject: Bayesian Model in Stan
parts:
Am currently trying to build a predictive model(logistic regression) using Stan, but in order to achieve better predictions, I thought it could be prudent to perform Bayesian Model Averaging by accounting for uncertainty in model selection as it is recommended by Hoeting 1999( https://projecteuclid.org/euclid.ss/1009212519#ui-tabs-1.)

But from literature this has not been attempted with success particularly in Bayesian paradigm. I have acquainted myself with the discussion in https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/stan-users/Bayesian$20model$20averaging$20without$20reversible-jump$20MCMC$20on$20highly-dimensional$20models%7Csort:relevance/stan-users/ixBFDRJj8Y0/Zag10wQlBQAJ and the general feeling is that BMA is almost impossible to do in Stan since it involves specification two priors, that is, parameter priors and model prior which are critical in computing marginal likelihood which is used to get posterior model probabilities (PMP).

Quick questions:

1. Is there anyone who has an alternative method whose results approximates that of BMA?

2. A snippet of Stan code that implement your suggestion in 1


Am trying to replicate the format of the result one would get when using R BMA package ( https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/BMA/BMA.pdf ) 

A

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Bayesian Model in Stan
parts:
Historically, model averaging was for situations where it was
infeasible computationally to build a mixture model or to expand
the model.

With Stan, you can just build the mixture model directly.
For snippets of code, see the mixture modeling chapter of
the Stan manual.

For extensive discussion, see the chapter of Gelman et al.'s
Bayesian Data Analysis on model comparison.

- Bob
